# `js/jsdoc-match-name`

**JSDoc tag names the project allows**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | no preset — name it in `[rules]` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `match` |
| **Fix** | `auto` — `codelaw fix` applies it; it never changes what the code does |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.2 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-jsdoc/match-name` |

## What it checks

The name a JSDoc tag gives (`@param {string} user_name`: `user_name`) is reported when it does not match `allowName` or does match `disallowName`, for the tags in `tags` (default every tag). Each check is an entry of `match` under a name of the project's choosing; an entry with neither `allowName` nor `disallowName` reports the first tag it applies to as a prohibited context, and `context` confines an entry to blocks documenting one kind of code. A name pattern is a regular expression, optionally written `/body/flags` (`i` is the only flag read). With `disallowName` and `replacement`, the disallowed part of the name is rewritten (`^_` with the empty string drops a leading underscore) and the finding is an automatic fix; otherwise it has none. `message` replaces the default. A `context` is a tree-sitter node kind of the code a block documents (`function_declaration`, `class_declaration`, `lexical_declaration`, `method_definition` …; the declaration under an `export`, and the function or class a variable holds, count too) or `any`. Upstream names these with esquery selectors over ESTree and the JSDoc AST, which have no equivalent here; a context here is a node kind, and what a block must hold is a `tag` it carries and a `matches` regular expression its text matches. eslint-plugin-jsdoc 65.4.2's `match-name`, read and reimplemented; where upstream reports that its `match` option is missing, this rule says nothing.

With no `match` set the rule is silent: it reports nothing, not even that the option is missing, and the engine does not run it on a single node. It is in no preset; a project switches it on by setting the option under `[rules]` (or in a `[scope.<name>]` for some files).

**Why:** A project that names its parameters one way wants the documentation to say the same.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**No preset turns it on.** Load its pack through any preset (`codelaw:js/recommended` here), then name the rule in `[rules]`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/recommended"]

[rules]
"js/jsdoc-match-name" = "error"
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/jsdoc-match-name" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `match` | `object` | `{}` | named checks, each `{ allowName, disallowName, replacement, tags, context, message }` |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-match-name"]
severity = "error"

[rules."js/jsdoc-match-name".options]
match = {}
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"js/jsdoc-match-name" = { severity = "error", options = { match = { camel = { allowName = "^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]*$", tags = ["param"] } } } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `match`

*object* · default `{}`

named checks, each `{ allowName, disallowName, replacement, tags, context, message }`

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-match-name".options]
match = { camel = { allowName = "^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]*$", tags = ["param"] } }
```

### Options in action

Each case below is one of the rule's tests (`packs/js/rules/js/jsdoc-match-name.cases.md`): the options, the input, and what codelaw reports.

#### a name that is not allowed

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-match-name".options]
match = { camel = { allowName = "^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]*$", tags = ["param"] } }
```

```js
/**
 * @param {string} user_name
 */
function find(user_name) {}
```

**Reports** at `2:20`.

#### a disallowed name with a replacement

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-match-name".options]
match = { p = { disallowName = "^_", replacement = "", tags = ["param"] } }
```

```js
/**
 * @param {string} _id
 * @param {string} [_name]
 */
function find(_id, _name) {}
```

**Reports** at `2:20`, `3:20`.

**After `codelaw fix`:**

```js
/**
 * @param {string} id
 * @param {string} [name]
 */
function find(_id, _name) {}
```

#### a context

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-match-name".options]
match = { p = { disallowName = "^_", tags = ["param"], context = "class_declaration" } }
```

```js
/**
 * @param {string} _a
 */
function f(_a) {}
/**
 * @param {string} _b
 */
class K {}
```

**Reports** at `6:20`.

#### another tag is not read

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-match-name".options]
match = { p = { disallowName = "^_", tags = ["param"] } }
```

```js
/**
 * @returns {string} _x
 */
function f() {}
```

**Reports nothing.**

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/jsdoc-match-name" = { options = { match = { camel = { allowName = "^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]*$", tags = ["param"] } } } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/jsdoc-match-name" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/jsdoc-match-name" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/jsdoc-match-name" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/jsdoc-match-name" = { severity = "warn", options = { match = { camel = { allowName = "^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]*$", tags = ["param"] } } } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/jsdoc-match-name": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"match": {"camel": {"allowName": "^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]*$", "tags": ["param"]}}}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/jsdoc-match-name: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/jsdoc-match-name expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/jsdoc-match-name --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/jsdoc-match-name       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/jsdoc-match-name  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>       # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

*With these options:* `{ match = { prop = { disallowName = "^_", replacement = "", tags = ["property"] } } }`

```js
/**
 * @typedef {object} User
 * @property {string} _id
 */
```

#### Do

*With these options:* `{ match = { prop = { disallowName = "^_", replacement = "", tags = ["property"] } } }`

```js
/**
 * @typedef {object} User
 * @property {string} id
 */
```

#### Fixed

*With these options:* `{ match = { prop = { disallowName = "^_", replacement = "", tags = ["property"] } } }`

```js
/**
 * @typedef {object} User
 * @property {string} id
 */
```
